blocks.text: CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update, and Delete and defines basic database actions. These operations are used to manage data stored in a database (as shown in Figure 4.4 and Table 4.1). Every database-based application depends on CRUD operations. They help maintain accurate and up-to-date information. Python uses SQL commands to perform these operations on databases.

blocks.alt: A table named students with columns ID, Name and Age and rows 1 Ibrahim 25; 2 Zainab 30; 3 Kiran 28. Four labelled buttons point at it: Create (INSERT...), Read (SELECT...), Update (UPDATE...) and Delete (DELETE...).
blocks.caption: Figure 4.4: Diagram showing Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations on a table (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 4.4).
Table 4.1: CRUD operations
rows: INSERT INTO students (ID, Name, Age) VALUES (1, 'John', 20);
Adds a new record to a table.
UPDATE students SET Age = 21 WHERE ID = 1;
Modifies an existing record in a table.
Removes a record from a table.
